Common patterns: use a hash as a frequency map (count chars/elements: str.chars.tally), use two pointers on a sorted array (see from both ends), use a hash for O(1) lookups (seen[x] to find a pair sum), use sliding window for subarrays (max sum of k consecutive). sections.title: Array & hash patterns
sections.content:
```ruby
# Frequency map: count characters
str = 'hello'
str.chars.tally                   # {'h'=>1, 'e'=>1, 'l'=>2, 'o'=>1}

# O(1) lookup: two-sum (find a pair that sums to target)
def two_sum(nums, target)
  seen = {}
  nums.each do |n|
    return [seen[target - n], n] if seen.key?(target - n)
    seen[n] = n
  end
  nil
end

# Two pointers on a sorted array (pair sum)
def two_sorted(nums, target)
  lo, hi = 0, nums.length - 1
  while lo < hi
    s = nums[lo] + nums[hi]
    return [nums[lo], nums[hi]] if s == target
    s < target ? lo += 1 : hi -= 1
  end
end

# Sliding window: max sum of k consecutive
def max_sum(nums, k)
  win = nums.first(k).sum
  best = win
  (k...nums.length).each do |i|
    win += nums[i] - nums[i - k]
    best = [best, win].max
  end
  best
end
```
